1.title: Short title, extent and commencement
1.summary: This Act may be called the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. It extends to the whole of India. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint.
keyPoints: Act extends to whole of India
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions
Different dates may be appointed for different States/UTs

2.title: Definitions
2.summary: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act including 'animal', 'animal article', 'Board', 'captive animal', 'Chief Wild Life Warden', 'Collector', 'dealer', 'forest officer', 'forest produce', 'hunting', 'livestock', 'manufacturer', 'meat', 'National Board', 'protected area', 'reserve forest', 'sanctuary', 'specified plant', 'taxidermy', 'trophy', 'vermin', 'wild animal', 'wild life', 'zoo', etc.
keyPoints: Animal includes mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, other chordates and invertebrates and their young and eggs
Hunting includes killing, poisoning, capturing, coursing, snaring, trapping, driving, baiting and attempts
Protected area includes National Park, sanctuary, conservation reserve, community reserve
Wild animal means any animal specified in Schedules I to IV found wild in nature
Vermin means any wild animal notified under section 62
Invasive alien species means species not native to India whose introduction may threaten wildlife (added 2022)
Scheduled specimen means specimen of species listed in CITES Appendices incorporated in Schedule IV (added 2022)

3.title: Appointment of Director and other officers
3.summary: The Central Government shall appoint a Director of Wild Life Preservation and such other officers and employees as may be necessary. They shall be subordinate to the Director.
keyPoints: Powers can be delegated with Central Government approval

4.title: Appointment of Chief Wild Life Warden and other officers
4.summary: The State Government shall appoint a Chief Wild Life Warden, Wild Life Wardens, and Honorary Wild Life Wardens. They shall be subordinate to the Chief Wild Life Warden.
keyPoints: Chief Wild Life Warden appointed by State Government
Honorary Wild Life Wardens can be appointed
All subordinate to Chief Wild Life Warden
Powers can be delegated with State Government approval

5.title: Power to delegate
5.summary: The Director may delegate powers to subordinate officers with Central Government approval. The Chief Wild Life Warden may delegate powers to subordinate officers with State Government approval (except powers under section 11(1)(a)).
keyPoints: Delegated powers have same effect as original

5A.title: Constitution of the National Board for Wild Life
5A.summary: The Central Government shall constitute the National Board for Wild Life with the Prime Minister as Chairperson, Minister of Forests as Vice-Chairperson, and members including MPs, NGOs, experts, Secretaries, Directors of key institutions, and Chief Wild Life Wardens.
keyPoints: Director of Wild Life Preservation is Member-Secretary
Term of non-ex-officio members prescribed by rules

5B.title: Standing Committee of the National Board
5B.summary: The National Board may constitute a Standing Committee consisting of the Vice-Chairperson, Member-Secretary, and up to 10 members nominated by the Vice-Chairperson. The Board may also constitute sub-committees and study groups.
keyPoints: Board can create sub-committees and study groups

5C.title: Functions of the National Board
5C.summary: The National Board promotes conservation and development of wild life and forests. It frames policies, advises governments, makes recommendations on protected areas, conducts impact assessments, reviews progress, and publishes status reports every two years.

6.title: Constitution of State Board for Wild Life
6.summary: State Government shall constitute a State Board for Wild Life with Chief Minister as Chairperson, Forest Minister as Vice-Chairperson, MLAs, NGO representatives, experts, Secretaries, department heads, and Chief Wild Life Warden as Member-Secretary.
keyPoints: 3 MLAs, 3 NGO reps, 10 experts (incl. 2 ST reps)
Chief Wild Life Warden is Member-Secretary
Must be constituted within 6 months of 2002 Amendment

7.title: Procedure to be followed by the Board
7.summary: The Board shall meet at least twice a year, regulate its own procedure including quorum. No act is invalid due to vacancy or defect in constitution.

8.title: Duties of State Board for Wild Life
8.summary: The State Board advises the State Government on selection and management of protected areas, policy formulation for wildlife and specified plants, amendment of Schedules, harmonising tribal needs with conservation, and other matters referred by State Government.

9.title: Prohibition of hunting
9.summary: No person shall hunt any wild animal specified in Schedule I, II, III, and IV (as amended by 2022: Schedules I and II only). Hunting is completely prohibited for these species.
keyPoints: Complete prohibition on hunting Schedule I & II species (2022 Amendment)
Earlier covered Schedules I, II, III, IV
Hunting includes killing, poisoning, capturing, trapping, etc.
Strictest protection for Schedule I & II species
9.penalties: See Section 51 - imprisonment 3-7 years, fine ₹25,000 - ₹1 lakh (higher for Schedule I/II)

11.title: Hunting of wild animals to be permitted in certain cases
11.summary: The Chief Wild Life Warden may permit hunting of Schedule I/II animals only if: (a) animal is dangerous to human life or property, or (b) animal is disabled/diseased beyond recovery. For Schedule III/IV: for education, research, scientific management. Permits are subject to conditions.
keyPoints: Schedule I/II: only for human safety or mercy killing
Schedule III/IV: for education, research, management
Permission only by Chief Wild Life Warden

12.title: Grant of permit for special purposes
12.summary: The Chief Wild Life Warden may grant permits for hunting for education, research, scientific management, collection of specimens for zoos/museums, derivation of snake venom for life-saving drugs. Permits have conditions and time limits.
keyPoints: Permits for education, research, scientific management
Subject to conditions and time limits

17A.title: Prohibition of picking, uprooting, etc. of specified plant
17A.summary: No person shall willfully pick, uproot, damage, destroy, acquire or collect any specified plant from any forest land or protected area. Possession, sale, transfer of such plants also prohibited.
keyPoints: Complete prohibition on specified plants (Schedule VI)
Applies to forest land and protected areas

18.title: Declaration of sanctuary
18.summary: State Government may declare any area (other than reserve forest/territorial waters) as a sanctuary if it has adequate ecological, faunal, floral, geomorphological, natural or zoological significance. Notification specifies boundaries.
keyPoints: Cannot include reserve forest (unless rights settled)

29.title: Destruction, etc., in a sanctuary prohibited without a permit
29.summary: No person shall destroy, exploit, remove wildlife/forest produce, divert habitat, set fire, use chemicals, or introduce exotic species in a sanctuary without a permit from Chief Wild Life Warden. Grazing/movement of livestock permitted under conditions.
keyPoints: Permit required from Chief Wild Life Warden
Prohibits: habitat destruction, fire, chemicals, exotic species

33.title: Control of sanctuaries
33.summary: The Chief Wild Life Warden shall control, manage and protect all sanctuaries in accordance with management plans approved by him as per Central Government guidelines. In Scheduled Areas, management plan prepared after consultation with Gram Sabha.
keyPoints: Chief Wild Life Warden controls sanctuaries
Management plans per Central Govt guidelines
Scheduled Areas: Gram Sabha consultation required
2022: 'manage and protect' instead of 'manage and maintain'

35.title: Declaration of National Parks
35.summary: State Government may declare an area as a National Park if it has ecological, faunal, floral, geomorphological, natural or zoological significance. Higher protection than sanctuary - no grazing, no habitat alteration. 2022: provisions of sections 27-33A apply immediately on declaration of intent.
keyPoints: 2022: interim protection on declaration of intent (section 35(3A))

36A.title: Declaration and management of a conservation reserve
36A.summary: State Government may declare government-owned areas as conservation reserves after consulting local communities. Central Government can also declare conservation reserves (2022). Management committee includes local representatives.
keyPoints: Declared by State Govt (or Central Govt post-2022)

36C.title: Declaration and management of community reserve
36C.summary: State Government may declare private/community land as community reserve if community agrees to protect wildlife. Management committee includes land owner, State Forest Dept rep, Panchayat/tribal rep. 2022: specific provisions for private land community reserves.
keyPoints: Committee includes owner, Forest Dept, Panchayat
2022: specific rules for private land reserves

38.title: Power of Central Government to declare areas as sanctuaries or National Parks
38.summary: Central Government can declare areas as sanctuaries or National Parks if State Government fails to act. 2022: Central Government can also declare conservation reserves. Applies same provisions as State declarations.
keyPoints: Central Govt can declare sanctuaries/National Parks
2022: Central Govt can declare conservation reserves
Same provisions as State declarations apply

38A.title: Constitution of Central Zoo Authority
38A.summary: Central Government constitutes Central Zoo Authority with Chairperson, members, Member-Secretary. Regulates zoos, grants recognition, sets standards for housing, upkeep, healthcare of animals.
keyPoints: Sets standards for animal housing, healthcare

38K.title: Definitions (Tiger Conservation)
38K.summary: Defines: National Tiger Conservation Authority, Steering Committee, Tiger Conservation Foundation, Tiger Reserve State, Tiger Reserve. Introduced by 2006 Amendment.
keyPoints: Tiger Reserve = area notified under section 38V
Tiger Conservation Foundation = established under section 38X

38L.title: Constitution of National Tiger Conservation Authority
38L.summary: Central Government constitutes NTCA with Minister of Environment as Chairperson, Minister of State as Vice-Chairperson, 3 MPs, 8 experts, Secretaries, DG Forests, Director WII, Director ZSI, Chief Wild Life Wardens (rotation), Member-Secretary. 2022: renamed to National Tiger Conservation Authority.
keyPoints: Chief Wild Life Wardens on rotation

38V.title: Tiger Conservation Plan
38V.summary: State Government prepares Tiger Conservation Plan for each tiger reserve: core/critical habitat (inviolate), buffer/peripheral area (co-existence). Must ensure ecological connectivity, livelihood needs, agricultural operations not incompatible. Voluntary relocation only with consent and rehabilitation.
keyPoints: Core area = inviolate for tiger conservation
No Scheduled Tribes displacement without rights settlement

38X.title: Establishment of Tiger Conservation Foundation
38X.summary: State Government establishes Tiger Conservation Foundation for each tiger reserve to facilitate ecological/economic/social development, promote eco-tourism, raise funds, support research and education. 2022: Chapter IVC renamed to 'Wild Life' from 'Tiger and Other Endangered Species'.

38Y.title: Constitution of Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
38Y.summary: Central Government constitutes Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (renamed from Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime Control Bureau in 2022) with Director of Wildlife Preservation as Director, and officers from Police, Customs, Forest, etc.
keyPoints: Officers from Police, Customs, Forest Depts

39.title: Wild animals, etc., to be Government property
39.summary: All wild animals (Schedule I-IV), animal articles, trophies, uncured trophies, meat, ivory imported into India, specified plants, and scheduled specimens (2022) are Government property. 2022: Live animals to be housed in recognized zoo/rescue centre. Disposal by Government (no commercial sale).
keyPoints: All Schedule I-IV animals = Govt property
Animal articles, trophies, meat, ivory = Govt property

40.title: Declarations
40.summary: Every person possessing captive animals, animal articles, trophies, uncured trophies, meat, ivory, specified plants must declare to Chief Wild Life Warden within 30 days. 2002: 'Part II of Schedule II' references removed. 2022: includes scheduled specimens.
keyPoints: Applies to captive animals, articles, trophies, meat, ivory

42.title: Certificate of ownership
42.summary: Chief Wild Life Warden issues certificate of ownership for lawfully possessed captive animals, animal articles, trophies. Required for transfer/transport. 2022: New section 42A allows voluntary surrender of captive animals/ivory with cancellation of certificate (no compensation).
keyPoints: Surrender = no compensation, property of State Govt

44.title: Dealings in trophy and animal articles without licence prohibited
44.summary: No person shall manufacture, deal in trophies/animal articles without licence. 1986 Amendment: Added Chapter VA for scheduled animals. Licence from Chief Wild Life Warden. Taxidermists also need licence. Peacock feather manufacturers exempted.
keyPoints: Issued by Chief Wild Life Warden

48A.title: Restriction on transportation of wild life
48A.summary: No person shall transport wild animals, animal articles, trophies, uncured trophies, meat, ivory, specified plants, scheduled specimens (2022) without permission. Transporter must have permit/transit pass. Vehicle can be seized.
keyPoints: Applies to animals, articles, trophies, meat, ivory, plants, scheduled specimens

49A.title: Definitions (Chapter VA)
49A.chapter: VA - Prohibition of Trade in Scheduled Animals
49A.summary: Defines: scheduled animal (Schedule I or Part II of Schedule II), scheduled animal article, specified date (2 months from commencement/addition). 2022: 'Part II of Schedule II' references removed throughout.
keyPoints: Scheduled animal = Schedule I or Part II of Schedule II
Scheduled animal article = article made from scheduled animal

49B.title: Prohibition of dealings in trophies, animal articles, etc., derived from scheduled animals
49B.chapter: VA - Prohibition of Trade in Scheduled Animals
49B.summary: After specified date, no person shall: manufacture/deal in scheduled animal articles, taxidermy scheduled animals, deal in trophies/uncured trophies from scheduled animals, deal in captive scheduled animals, deal in/serve meat from scheduled animals. Exemptions for Govt corporations, taxidermy for Govt/education with permission.
keyPoints: Complete trade ban after specified date
Licences before specified date don't authorize

49M.title: Possession, transfer and breeding of living scheduled animal species
49M.summary: Every person possessing living Schedule IV animal must report to Management Authority. Authority may issue registration certificate. Transfers, births, deaths must be reported. No possession/transfer/breeding except per this section. 2022: New Chapter VB for CITES implementation.
keyPoints: Transfers, births, deaths must be reported
Breeding of Appendix I species requires licence (49N)
Central Govt can exempt certain species/quantities

50.title: Power of entry, search, arrest and detention
50.chapter: VI - Prevention and Detection of Offences
50.summary: Authorized officers (Director, Chief Wild Life Warden, police, forest officers, customs, coast guard - 2022) can enter, search, arrest without warrant, seize. 2022: Added Management Authority officers, customs officers, coast guard officers. Schedules specimen added to seizure items.
keyPoints: Officers: Director, CWLW, police, forest, customs, coast guard
Seizure of animals, articles, trophies, scheduled specimens
50.penalties: Enabling provision - see Section 51 for offences

51.title: Penalties
51.chapter: VI - Prevention and Detection of Offences
51.summary: General penalty: imprisonment 3-7 years, fine ₹1 lakh (increased from ₹25,000 in 2022). For Schedule I/II/Appendix I Schedule IV: imprisonment 3-7 years, fine ₹25,000 (increased from ₹10,000 in 2002, ₹25,000 in 2022). Second offence: 7 years, fine ₹5 lakh (increased from ₹25,000 in 2022). Section 51A (Chapter VA): 1-7 years, fine ₹5,000+. Section 51C (Tiger Reserve): 3-7 years, fine ₹50,000-2 lakh (first), 7 years, fine ₹5-50 lakh (subsequent).
keyPoints: Section 54: Compounding up to ₹5 lakh (2022: was ₹25,000)
51.penalties: See above - this IS the penalty section

51A.title: Certain conditions to apply while granting bail
51A.chapter: VI - Prevention and Detection of Offences
51A.summary: For offences under Chapter VA (scheduled animals) or relating to Schedule I/II/Appendix I Schedule IV: bail only if Public Prosecutor heard, court satisfied accused not guilty and not likely to commit offence on bail. 2022: Added Appendix I Schedule IV.
keyPoints: Strict bail conditions for serious offences
Court must be satisfied accused not guilty
Applies to Chapter VA, Schedule I/II, Appendix I Schedule IV
51A.penalties: Bail condition - not a penalty itself

55.title: Cognizance of offences
55.chapter: VI - Prevention and Detection of Offences
55.summary: Court can take cognizance only on complaint by: Director, Chief Wild Life Warden, authorized officer, Management Authority (2022), Wildlife Crime Control Bureau officer (2002), or person giving 60-day notice. 2022: Added Management Authority and WCCB officers.

62.title: Declaration of certain wild animals to be vermin
62.summary: Central Government may declare wild animals (except Schedule I/II) as vermin for any area/period. 2022: Changed from 'other than Schedule I and Part II Schedule II' to 'specified in Schedule II'. Declared animals deemed NOT in Schedule II for that area/period.
keyPoints: 2022: Only Schedule II animals (was Schedules III-V)
Declared animals removed from Schedule II protection
62.penalties: Vermin hunting = no penalty under Act
